titulo: Without the ice, with the lot, and one of those
subtitulo: The two words that get you the food you actually want — and the one word that opens a bakery, a market stall, a hotel desk and a chemist
cena: Thirty-four degrees, a terrace table, and the tall glass the waiter has just put down in front of you is three quarters frozen water.

clique.desconto: Nobody taught you those four sentences. You built them, just now, out of one.
clique.piso: Four sentences you did not learn, from one you did. Most people who spend a fortnight in Spain never build a single one.

frasePiso: Four sentences you did not learn, from one you did. Most people who spend a fortnight in Spain never build a single one.
permissao: You never have to explain why. 'Sin hielo' is a whole sentence on its own — no reason, no apology, no story. And when you do not know the noun, point and say quería; they will finish it for you.
espelho: Apologising before you correct a drink is the bit that reads as odd there. Nobody apologises for it, because as far as the bar is concerned nothing has happened yet.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You say 'sin hielo', and the glass lands on the table full of it anyway.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: He got it wrong and I made him get it wrong. If I say anything now I am the difficult foreigner.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: At a counter the drink is not finished until you have taken it — sending it straight back is a step in the transaction, not a complaint about anyone. Ice is also one of the extras a bar is allowed to charge for, so it is a line item, not a favour.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Slide it back across the counter, say 'sin hielo, por favor' once more, and keep your face friendly. No apology, no explanation.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You find out that correcting an order there is routine and free, and after that you order what you actually want for the rest of the fortnight.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not at a bar three deep at midnight, where nobody is going to redo anything — there you drink it and say the two words earlier next time.

steps.pt: Warm-up, ten seconds. Metronome hand: one tap a syllable, all the same size. Sin-hie-lo. Three equal taps.

steps.promptPt: Yesterday's bar, same barman, same second and a half of his attention. Everyone along the counter is holding the same short glass. Order that. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh POH-nehs OO-nah KAH-nyah, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: a small draught beer
Thirty-four degrees. A terrace table. The waiter puts down a tall glass, and three quarters of it is frozen water.
You are not going to send that one back. You are going to stop it happening to the next one.
Here is the frame, and it is two syllables. Sin — without. Con — with. Para — for. No verb anywhere.
The frame stays put. The thing that comes after it is the only part that ever moves. Carmen.

steps.pinyin: seen YEH-loh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Without ice, please.
Same two syllables, new thing on the end. Emilio, at the same table, with the water bottle.

steps.pinyin: seen gahs, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Still, please. (literally: without gas)

steps.promptPt: Second day, same terrace, same waiter, and you would like the next one to be a drink rather than a snowball. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: seen YEH-loh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: without it

steps.promptPt: A sandwich counter at eight in the morning. Your train goes in twelve minutes and the man has just reached for a plate and a fork. You are not sitting down. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: PAH-rah yeh-BAR, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: to go, not here
Now one that answers you back. He asks a question, and one word closes it.

steps.pinyin: PAH-rah KWAN-tohs
steps.pt: 👂 'For how many?' — the door question. Hold up fingers if you have to, but you won't have to.

steps.promptPt: A restaurant door at half nine, a man with a pile of menus under his arm, and he has just asked you exactly that. You, and the person standing next to you. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: PAH-rah dohs, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: for two
One more, and it is the one that pays for the app. The card machine turns round and offers you pounds.
Say yes to that and you pay ten to thirteen per cent over the euro price. Two syllables stop it.

steps.promptPt: The waiter is holding the machine out and the screen is offering you a total in pounds, which is the only number on it you understand. Press the button you do not understand, and tell him. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: seen kon-behr-SYON
steps.pt: in euros, then

steps.es: Ay, perdona, ya le he dado. Lo anulo y lo hago otra vez.
steps.pinyin: ai, pehr-DOH-nah, yah leh eh DAH-dhoh. loh ah-NOO-loh ee loh AH-goh OH-trah beth
steps.pt: 👂 'Sorry, I already pressed it. I'll cancel and do it again.' — saying it out loud is what makes him cancel.
steps.tts: Ay, perdona, ya le he dado. Lo anulo y lo hago otra vez.

steps.pt: Two syllables, every card payment of the fortnight, at the real price. That is the frame earning its keep.
You can order a beer. Now the woman behind the counter is waiting, and what you want is not a beer.
One word does it. Quería. keh-REE-ah. Not 'I want' — softer. 'I was after…'. Carmen first.

steps.es: Quería un café con leche, por favor.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah oon kah-FEH kon LEH-cheh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: I'd like a white coffee, please.
steps.tts: Quería un café con leche, por favor.

steps.pt: Hear the seam? Quería, and then the thing. Same word, different thing — listen to her do it.

steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah lah KAR-tah, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: I'd like the menu, please.
The thing on the end changed. Quería did not. It never will. Now you.

steps.promptPt: The bakery, nine in the morning. The thing you want is behind glass and nobody has ever told you its name. Point, and start. Speak now.
steps.es: Quería uno de esos, por favor.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah OO-noh deh EH-sohs, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: that one there

steps.promptPt: Different morning, same bakery, and today you are buying for the person you travel with, who has not eaten wheat since they were twelve. Everything behind that glass is made of it. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: ai AL-goh seen GLOO-ten
steps.pt: anything at all without it

steps.promptPt: Saturday, the market stall. The scoop is already in her hand, four people are queueing behind you, and what you want is the box of red things in front of her. Half a kilo. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah MEH-dhyoh KEE-loh deh toh-MAH-tehs
steps.pt: half a kilo of them

steps.promptPt: Midnight, the hotel desk. Your window gives onto the square and the square has a band in it. Ask him to move you. Speak now.
steps.es: Quería otra habitación, si es posible.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah OH-trah ah-bee-tah-THYOHN, see es poh-SEE-bleh
steps.pt: somewhere else, if possible

steps.encaixe: algo para las quemaduras del sol
steps.promptPt: The chemist. You have no idea of the word for what two hours on the beach did to your shoulders — but you know how the sentence starts, and you know what you want it to do. Speak now.
steps.es: Quería algo para las quemaduras del sol.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah AL-goh PAH-rah lahs keh-mah-DOO-rahs del sol
steps.pt: something for what the sun did
It survives contact. Listen to what comes back at the desk, and to how little of it you need.

steps.es: Quería otra habitación, si es posible.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah OH-trah ah-bee-tah-THYOHN, see es poh-SEE-bleh
steps.pt: — I'd like a different room, if that's possible.

steps.pinyin: leh eem-POR-tah OO-nah PLAHN-tah mahs AHL-tah
steps.pt: — Would a higher floor be alright?

steps.pinyin: meh-KHOR toh-dhah-BEE-ah — GRAH-thyahs
steps.pt: — Even better. Thank you.
GUIRI ALERT. Quería takes a thing. A coffee, a room, half a kilo of something.
Hang a plan off the back of it — move my booking to the other hotel and then — and you have left the runway.
Want a thing: quería. Want an action: point, and say the thing anyway. They'll meet you halfway.
Two more, and both of them happen sitting down. The first one catches everybody on day one.
GUIRI ALERT. You sit down, you smile, you say 'el menú, por favor'. And lunch arrives.
'El menú' is a set meal at a fixed price. The list of everything they cook is 'la carta'. And nobody corrects you.

steps.pinyin: nohs TRAH-eh lah KAR-tah, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Could we have the menu, please?

steps.promptPt: You've been sat down at a table and given nothing to read. Ask for the menu — the real one, the list of everything. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: nohs TRAH-eh lah KAR-tah, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: the list of everything
Four words decide how much food lands. Tapa, small. Pincho, on bread, paid one by one. Ración, a plate for the middle of the table. Media ración, half of one.

steps.es: ¿Esto es tapa, media ración o ración?
steps.pinyin: EHS-toh es TAH-pah, MEH-dhyah rrah-THYON oh rrah-THYON
steps.pt: Is this a small one, a half or a full one?
steps.tts: ¿Esto es tapa, media ración o ración?

steps.promptPt: There is a name chalked on the board that you cannot picture at all, and you are one nod away from ordering four more of them. Find out how big it is first. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Esto es tapa, media ración o ración?
steps.pinyin: EHS-toh es TAH-pah, MEH-dhyah rrah-THYON oh rrah-THYON
steps.pt: how big is this one

steps.es: Eso es ración. Es grande, ¿eh? Es para compartir.
steps.pinyin: EH-soh es rrah-THYON. es GRAN-deh, eh. es PAH-rah kom-par-TEER
steps.pt: 👂 'That's a full plate — big, mind. It's for sharing.' — the answer you needed before it landed, not after.
steps.tts: Eso es ración. Es grande, ¿eh? Es para compartir.

steps.promptPt: Two of you, one plate in the middle, everybody else in the room eating the same way. Order a full plate of ham and tell him what it is for. Speak now.
steps.es: Ponnos una ración de jamón para compartir.
steps.pinyin: POH-nohs OO-nah rrah-THYON deh khah-MOHN PAH-rah kom-par-TEER
steps.pt: for the middle of the table

steps.promptPt: Your friend just ordered something at speed and it sounded good. The waiter turns to you. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: loh MEES-moh PAH-rah MEE
steps.pt: the same, this end
And when the plate is nearly right, you hand the kitchen the same two syllables through the waiter.

steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-dheh ah-THEHR seen theh-BOH-yah
steps.pt: Could you do it for me without onion?

steps.promptPt: The dish you want has one thing in it that you have hated since you were nine, and it is the sort of thing a kitchen can leave out. Ask them to. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-dheh ah-THEHR seen theh-BOH-yah
steps.pt: made without it

steps.es: Es que ya viene hecho. Se la quito por encima, si quieres.
steps.pinyin: es keh yah BYEH-neh EH-choh. seh lah KEE-toh por en-THEE-mah, see KYEH-rehs
steps.pt: 👂 'It comes ready-made — I can take it off the top.' — half a yes, and it is worth taking.
steps.tts: Es que ya viene hecho. Se la quito por encima, si quieres.

steps.pt: Steak. Three words, no frame needed. Poco hecho, al punto, muy hecho. Rare, medium, well done.

steps.es: Poco hecho, por favor. / Al punto. / Muy hecho.
steps.pinyin: POH-koh EH-choh · al POON-toh · mwee EH-choh
steps.pt: 👂 Rare, please. / Medium. / Well done. — the list is the list, and it is said when you order, not when it lands.
steps.tts: Poco hecho, por favor. Al punto. Muy hecho.

steps.pt: Spain cooks meat further than Britain does unless told otherwise, and the telling goes in with the order.

steps.pinyin: al POON-toh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Medium, please.

Straight back over the bar, two syllables again, friendly face, no apology. Nothing has gone wrong yet.
Not at a bar three deep at midnight, mind. There you drink it, and you say it earlier next time.

Count them. The bakery, the market stall, the hotel desk, the chemist. Four places, one word.

Shadowing. Out loud, with them, equal taps. The two that change the most days:

steps.pinyin: seen YEH-loh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Without ice, please.

steps.es: Quería algo para las quemaduras del sol.
steps.pinyin: keh-REE-ah AL-goh PAH-rah lahs keh-mah-DOO-rahs del sol
steps.pt: I'd like something for sunburn.
One last one out loud, and then you are done. A counter we have not stood at yet.

steps.promptPt: Nine at night, the ice cream counter, and you are walking to the station with it in your hand. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: PAH-rah yeh-BAR, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: not eating it here
That is it. Two frames, six counters, and nothing you had to look up. Next: the one sentence you say slowly. Hasta luego.

aprofundar.titulo: Two frames, and why you were never given a table (optional reading)

secoes.corpo: All three are understood. 'Quiero' is fine and slightly blunt; 'quería' is what you actually hear across a Spanish counter, and it costs you no extra syllables. 'Me gustaría' is the one your schoolbook taught and the one we have deliberately left out: it is padding, it takes longer to say, and the British habit of stacking padding in front of a request is exactly what stops you being served. The useful thing about 'quería' is not politeness at all — it is that it says nothing about the person you are talking to. You never have to decide whether this is a 'tú' situation or an 'usted' one, and that decision is the one an English speaker gets wrong under pressure.

exemplos.pt: keh-REE-ah oon ah-dhap-tah-DOR deh en-CHOO-feh — I'd like a plug adaptor. (a word you have never said in your life, in a sentence you already own)
keh-REE-ah dohs bee-YEH-tehs PAH-rah seh-BEE-yah — I'd like two tickets to Seville. (same word, ticket office)

secoes.corpo: Two words, no verb, and they work as complete utterances: 'Sin hielo, por favor.' is a finished sentence. 'Sin' takes anything you want left out — gluten, gas, cebolla, hielo, conversión. 'Con' takes anything you want added — hielo, limón, leche. 'Para' is the widest of the three: it takes a purpose ('para llevar'), a number ('para dos'), a person ('para mí') and a document ('para el seguro' — the receipt for the insurance claim, which is the version of this frame you will be most grateful for). The one that pays: 'sin conversión' at a card machine. Under Regulation (EU) 2019/518, in force since April 2020, the machine has to disclose its markup over the European Central Bank rate before you accept, and the markups reported in 2026 sit at roughly ten to thirteen per cent. The rule of thumb is easier than the arithmetic: the option shown in your own currency is the wrong one.

exemplos.pt: meh loh POH-neh PAH-rah yeh-BAR — Could you put it up to take away? (the two frames stacked)

exemplos.es: Quería la factura para el seguro.
exemplos.pt: keh-REE-ah lah fak-TOO-rah PAH-rah el seh-GOO-roh — I'd like the receipt for the insurance.

secoes.titulo: 'La carta', 'el menú', and the four sizes
secoes.corpo: 'El menú' is a set meal at a fixed price; 'la carta' is the list of everything the kitchen can make. Two more on the same page: 'entrada' is a starter, not the entrance, and 'tortilla' is a thick potato omelette, not a flatbread. On sizes: a 'tapa' is a small plate that comes with a drink; a 'pincho' or 'montadito' is the northern version on a slice of bread, paid by the unit; a 'ración' is a full sharing plate and genuinely large; a 'media ración' is half of one, which for two people is usually right. In the Basque Country the 'pintxo' system is different again: you help yourself from the bar top and the cocktail sticks on your plate are the bill, so you keep them. And 'S.M.' or 'según mercado' beside seafood means the price depends on weight and the market that morning — ask before you order.

exemplos.pt: KWAN-toh KWEHS-tah AN-tehs deh peh-DEER-loh — How much is it before I order it?
KWAN-tohs pah-LEE-yohs TYEH-nehs — 👂 'How many sticks have you got?' — he is not accusing you of anything, he is adding up.
